plain_english: How tell what cannot be named? If anyone reaches it at all, it is by the honest method of feeling oneself.
sanskrit_cite: vyapadeśavihīnasya tattvasya kathanaṃ katham / svasaṃvedanasadyuktyā gamyate yadi kenacit

plain_english: Taught the yoga of knowing, yet with no trust inside — trustless, how could he ever taste freedom's fruit?
sanskrit_cite: jñānayogopadeśena yasya nāśvāsa āntaraḥ / samāśvāsavihīnatvāt kathaṃ naiḥśreyasaṃ phalam

plain_english: The way to the goal is this: stay awake in your own awakening. From such waking the sage stands whole, undivided.
sanskrit_cite: upeyaprāptyupāyo 'yaṃ svabodhe jāgarūkatā / svabodhajāgarūkatvān nirvibhāgā sthitir muneḥ

plain_english: No way but keeping to your own being. Keep to her, rest in yourself — whoever does is happy.
sanskrit_cite: upāyo nāparaḥ kaścit svasattānugamād ṛte / tām evānusaran yogī svastho yaḥ sa sukhī bhavet

plain_english: From noticing your own notions, from holding to pure knowing, from winning the highest joy — the sage grows one solid mass of waking.
sanskrit_cite: svasaṃkalpaparāmarśād viśuddhajñānasaṃśrayāt / paramāhlādalābhāc ca bodhaikaghanatā muneḥ

plain_english: Grip your notions still, and power comes to rest in the powerful; their oneness is what yogis are after.
sanskrit_cite: nigṛhīte svasaṃkalpe śakteḥ śaktimati sthitiḥ / śaktiśaktimator aikyam ity upeyaṃ ca yoginām

plain_english: Know your own form, drop the veil of principles, scatter the cause of striving — then, tradition says, you are called free.
sanskrit_cite: prāpte svarūpavijñāne santyakte tattvakañcuke / udyogakāraṇe kīrṇe muktaḥ sa kila kathyate

plain_english: With a fully wakened mind, hold to waking alone — until, by your own strength, you stand in yourself, alone.
sanskrit_cite: bodhamātre grahaḥ kāryaḥ suprabuddhena cetasā / tāvad yāvat svasāmarthyāt svaniṣṭhaḥ kevalo bhavet
